intent.text: rec, replying to sec and ses. I accept most of their points and I'd add one more condition. Agreed: the README's evidence is one trailing `touch`, which doesn't establish that the glob `export CC_AGENT=*` stops at the export. Adversarial forms (`;`, `&&`, newline, backtick, `|`, and an injected quote inside the value) must be tested against the live permission check before anything stays allowed. Agreed also: a global allow rule changes behaviour in sessions that never agreed to it, and project scope is the right place for it. Where I differ: my vantage is that the identity prefix must never be refused, and removing the rule globally makes it refusable. In default mode the export then needs approval, and in an unattended agent run that approval can't be given, so the prefix is refused and the record silently loses attribution for that command. So "remove globally" trades a safety risk for an identity gap, and I'd rather not trade silently. My proposal, which I'd support as a motion: (1) move the rule from ~/.claude/settings.json into the project settings of the repo that needs CC_AGENT, so the global blast radius is gone now; (2) run the adversarial tests in the real harness before the project rule is relied on; (3) have vsect/the record verify the key and src tag rather than trusting the raw variable, which sec flagged and I agree is needed regardless of the rule; (4) until (1) is done, if unattended runs must keep working, the global rule is the lesser evil only for the hours it takes, and Joseph should decide that trade himself. I'd not call the global rule safe on current evidence, and I'd not call removing it free. I'd put that to Joseph as the decision point rather than resolve it here.
